# Copilot Instructions — MarginIQ (Intel CCG CVE Memory RMT Margin Analysis Tool)

This repository contains MarginIQ, a project-agnostic Windows Python tool that extracts `START_RMT`
(Rank Margin Tool) blocks from Intel MRC debug logs and produces CSV, Excel,
HTML (incl. DDR5 Mode Register and ODT tabs), PowerPoint and optional JMP Pro charts.

## Running the tool from chat

When the user asks to plot, chart, analyze or report RMT margins, follow the
[rmt-margin-plots skill](skills/rmt-margin-plots/SKILL.md). In short:

- Use `<repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` (created by `setup.bat`), never bare `python`.
- Run only `rmt_log_pipeline.py` (directly, or via `marginiq.cmd`, which wraps it with the
  repo `.venv`), always with `--no-ask-chart-approval`.
- Never launch `rmt_gui.py`, `Launch_RMT_GUI.bat`, `MarginIQ.lnk` or `rmt_pipeline_runner.py` —
  they are interactive and will hang an agent session.
- To *open* a guide in the browser when the user asks (user guide, CLI / automation guide,
  spec-limits table, …), run `<repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe <repo>\rmt_help.py <page>`
  (`readme|quickstart|cli|install|pipeline|projects`); it does not block. For how-to
  questions, answer from the `.md` guides instead of opening a browser.
- If `.venv` is missing run `setup.bat --no-prompt` (never plain `setup.bat`, which asks
  shortcut questions).
- Never invent input/output paths; ask the user.
- Pass `--project` (key from `projects.json`, e.g. `NVL`, `WCL`); ask the user when
  the project cannot be inferred unambiguously.
- Resolve every path from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; never hardcode
  user-specific paths.
- If the pipeline prints `[MarginIQ update] …`, tell the user to `git pull`;
  don't pull on their behalf unless asked.

## Editing the code

- Keep the tool self-contained: no imports or file references outside this
  repository other than the pinned packages in `requirements.txt`, the Python
  standard library, and the user's own JMP Pro install.
- Add any new third-party dependency to `requirements.txt` with a pinned version.
- Use `pathlib.Path` for file paths and f-strings for formatting; keep Python
  3.10 compatibility.
- File I/O must handle `FileNotFoundError` / `PermissionError` with clear messages;
  `subprocess` calls must check return codes and must not use `shell=True`.
- Keep the documented exit codes (0-5) stable — the agent skill and
  [CLI_AUTOMATION.md](../CLI_AUTOMATION.md) integrations depend on them; keep its console
  messages and `rmt_metadata.json` keys in sync with the code.
- Product name, subtitle and version live in `rmt_project.py`; platforms live in
  `projects.json` — never hardcode a project name (e.g. Nova Lake) in code. Platform
  behaviour (block markers, `require_rmt_task`, `dtr`, `platform_variants`, `rmt_limits`)
  belongs in `projects.json`; NVL must stay on the built-in defaults.
- The app icon is generated by `scripts/make_icon.py` (`assets/marginiq.ico` / `.png`);
  shortcuts are made by `scripts/create_shortcuts.ps1` and share the AppUserModelID
  `Intel.CCG.CVE.MarginIQ` with `rmt_gui.py` — keep them in sync.
